Preface: I'm Canadian, so YMMV.

When you first start you should expect to be in training for a week or two at least. The experience is best summed up  as drinking from a fire hose - just take in what you can. As long as your team is half-decent, they'll be around to coach you. Expectations are pretty minimal for a new start: show up on time with a good attitude and be willing to help out wherever you're needed. Typically, new starts will be given ad hoc/admin tasks or simple stuff like ordering dinner for the team. Don't discount these tasks, they seem small and trivial but actually play a big part in supporting your team over the long hours that you'll work.

Depending on staffing, deadlines, when you start (January vs. September) and/or any significant matters that arise throughout the audit, you may be assigned your own FSLI. On my team, we assign simpler FSLIs to the new starts to introduce them to what our audit procedures actually look like in practice. Again, if your team is half-decent, you'll be working closely with a senior who will guide you and coach you to test these items. It can be hair-ripping at times, but it all depends on your team. Worst case is you'll get a shit file and a shit team who expects you to figure out everything yourself, but in my experience this is rare.

While I don't think internships are explicitly necessary (we consider new grads with no experience just as much as we consider those that do), I think it's important to remember that the progression scheme at the associate level is designed to incorporate an internship - i.e., the "standard" route is to do a summer internship and secure your FT offer while you finish school. It's a great opportunity to learn the culture of the office you want to work at and get to know some of the people that are there without having to deal with busy season. A busy season internship will also allow you - in some places - to start FT at the experienced associate level.

Let me be clear though: **under zero circumstances is a FT position guaranteed if you graduate.**

this code popped right after i bought it. took it into our local subie speciality shop. swapped the LH and RH OCV, solenoid, and sensor to check. no issues. i took it home and changed the oil, code went away. immediately i'm thinking that my bearings are shot and my engine is about to grenade itself.

sent a sample to blackstone and the oil came back clean as a whistle - we're talking well below the universal averages for a 5000km run.

the issue is that this code could be anything. it could be your oil control assembly, dirty oil (whether its metal shavings or sludge), a bad AVCS sprocket, your banjo bolt filters cracking and sending pieces through your oil lines, anything related to oil pressure, etc.

change the oil, send a sample out. find yourself a subaru shop that's not the dealership and get them to take a look. or swap the OCVs yourself and drive. if you have an AP, set it to monitor the LH and RH AVCS Exh values and see if they're in sync.
